title: Superannuation Guarantee (Administration) Amendment (Frontline Emergency Service Workers) Bill 2025
short_title: Superannuation Guarantee (Administration) Amendment (Frontline Emergency Service Workers) Bill 2025

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would lift the superannuation guarantee rate for firefighters and paramedics by an extra 4.4 per cent to match the base rate paid to Australian Defence Force personnel.

It would amend the Superannuation Guarantee (Administration) Act 1992 so that an employer's charge percentage for a firefighter or paramedic employee includes an additional 4.4, taking the rate to 16.4 per cent.

The higher rate would apply to quarters starting on or after 1 July 2025, directly covering the Commonwealth except Norfolk Island, the Northern Territory, the Australian Capital Territory and the non-government sector, with no immediate effect in Victoria, Norfolk Island and some other state schemes.
changes: A new paragraph 19(1)(aa) would add 4.4 to the charge percentage used to work out an employer's superannuation guarantee shortfall for a firefighter or paramedic employee.
New definitions of firefighting duties, paramedic duties, firefighter employee and paramedic employee would be inserted into subsection 6(1) of the Act.
A new section 15AA would set out who counts as a firefighter employee and who counts as a paramedic employee.
The bill would commence the day after Royal Assent but would have no practical effect until 1 July 2025.
summary.affected: Firefighters, paramedics and their employers covered by the superannuation guarantee are affected, including those in the Commonwealth other than Norfolk Island, the Northern Territory, the Australian Capital Territory and the non-government sector.

speeches.speaker: Malcolm Roberts
speeches.brief: Moved to suspend standing orders and restore the Australian Education Legislation Amendment (Prohibiting the Indoctrination of Children) Bill 2020 and twelve other listed bills to the Notice Paper for consideration at the second reading stage; both questions were agreed to.
